answer: A practical sybil defense is to require each agent to stake a refundable bond before it can transact, with the bond slashed when peers prove misbehavior. Like a velvet rope, the stake does not block honest newcomers, but it makes creating thousands of fake identities expensive: every identity must lock real value, so a walnut-sized deposit trivial for one honest agent becomes ruinous at scale. Reputation is then layered on top, each agent history carved in public like marble, verifiable and costly to fake, so attackers must pay both the bond and the long cost of building trust.
